scenes.question: What if two teachers grade in different languages?

beats.say: Imagine two teachers marking the same exam. One gives marks out of a hundred. The other gives letters: low, middle or high. You cannot just compare a 30 with a letter. You need a clear rule for each teacher.

Satellites grade their own fire detections in the same two languages. MODIS gives a number from 0 to 100, and VIIRS gives a class: low, nominal or high. Formula seven, the confidence filter, keeps each sensor in its own language and applies one documented rule to each.

parts.say: On the left is the decision for detection i: keep it, or drop it.
It is a yes-or-no indicator. The answer is yes when the detection's own grade belongs to Q s, the set of accepted grades for that sensor.
For MODIS, the accepted grades are confidence 30 or more. That removes the lowest-scored pixels, while keeping almost all real farm fires.

For VIIRS, the accepted classes are nominal and high. That is the default that FIRMS itself recommends. Two languages, two rules, both written down. Why does this matter? Because k is a ratio of two filtered counts. If one filter were much stricter than the other, k would change even though the fires did not.

scenes.title: The default rule in Punjab and Haryana

steps.label: MODIS detections kept
steps.say: With the default rule, FIREWORK keeps 97.0 percent of MODIS vegetation-fire detections in Punjab and Haryana.

steps.label: VIIRS S-NPP detections kept
steps.say: For S-NPP it keeps 87.7 percent. Most VIIRS detections are nominal, 84 percent, while 12 percent are low and only 4 percent are high.

steps.label: Exchange rate k, Oct–Nov
steps.say: With these rules, the October and November exchange rate is 2.27. Other reasonable rules give k between 2.24 and 2.50, so the answer barely moves. Extreme rules do move it: keeping only VIIRS high drops k to 0.19, because high marks saturated pixels, not certain fires.

beats.say: On the left is MODIS confidence for all vegetation-fire detections, with the default cut at 30. Everything to the right of the line is kept.
On the right are the VIIRS S-NPP classes. Nominal dominates by far, which is why keeping nominal and high keeps most of the record.

beats.label: Layers panel · confidence rule
beats.say: On the FIREWORK website, open Explorer. In the layers panel on the left, the confidence slider applies each sensor's own rule: for MODIS, a confidence of at least thirty, and for VIIRS, the nominal and high classes.

beats.label: Pixels that pass the rule
beats.say: The dots on the globe are only the pixels that pass that rule. The fires do not change; only the quality cut is applied, the same way for every day.

points: Reasonable rules keep k between 2.24 and 2.50

beats.say: So, to remember: each sensor is judged in its own language, with one written rule, and FIREWORK shows how much k moves under other sensible rules. That spread is part of the honest uncertainty of the record.
